title: The reins of the midbrain: Task-based habenula function in healthy humans
title_zh: 中脑的缰绳：健康人群任务范式下缰核功能
abstract: The habenula is a small epithalamic structure that animal models have characterized as a key node linking value-laden information to midbrain monoaminergic systems. Its involvement in mood disorders has driven growing interest in characterizing its function in humans, yet the healthy baseline of habenular function measured using task-based fMRI has not been systematically synthesised. Thus, we searched PubMed, Scopus, and PsycINFO and identified 34 task-based fMRI studies (37 cohorts, N = 1480) examining habenular function in healthy adults. To address the methodological challenges of habenular imaging, we appraised each study through a spatial specificity framework. Findings were synthesised across four functional domains: affective and sensory processing, computational signalling, cognitive-affective regulation, and circadian rhythms. The human habenula emerged as a multifunctional integrative node that pulls back on - or modulates - midbrain function, much like the reins from which it takes its name. It processed primary and secondary aversive stimuli, encoded the predictive value of aversive cues, and signalled negative prediction errors across reinforcer types. Research also linked habenula activity to response gating under conflict and threat, and to higher-order cognitive processes. These responses recruited distributed circuits in which cortical inputs drive habenular modulation of midbrain monoaminergic function. Based on our framework, the most rigorous findings involved action gating under threat, foraging paradigms, and Pavlovian aversive conditioning, whereas foundational findings on primary aversion and reward prediction error encoding are starting to be replicated with more appropriate protocols. We recommend systematic adoption of high-specificity protocols and the integration of laterality and sex as biological variables.
abstract_zh: 缰核是一个小型上丘脑后部结构，动物模型将其刻画为连接价值相关信息与中脑单胺能系统的关键节点。其在情绪障碍中的参与推动了对人类缰核功能的研究兴趣，但健康个体中基于任务范式fMRI测得的缰核基线功能尚未被系统综合。因此，我们检索了PubMed、Scopus与PsycINFO，识别出34项任务范式fMRI研究（37个队列，N = 1480），考察健康成年人的缰核功能。为应对缰核影像学的技术挑战，我们通过空间特异性框架评估了每项研究。结果在四个功能域中综合：情绪与感觉加工、计算性信号传递、认知-情绪调节与昼夜节律。人类缰核表现为多功能的整合性节点，能够抑制或调节中脑功能，类似其名称“缰绳”所示。它处理初级和次级厌恶刺激，编码厌恶线索的预测价值，并跨奖励类型信号化负向预测误差。研究还发现，缰核活动与冲突与威胁下的反应门控及更高阶认知过程相关。这些反应动员了分布式通路，其中皮层输入驱动缰核对中脑单胺能功能的调节。基于我们的框架，最严谨的证据来自威胁下动作门控、觅食范式与巴甫洛夫厌恶条件化，而关于初级厌恶和奖励预测误差编码的基础性发现正开始在更适当的范式中重复出现。我们建议系统采用高特异性协议，并将半球优势和性别整合为生物学变量。
